text: Parasites live either inside the body (internal parasites) or on/in the skin (external parasites), and are generally harmful — controlling them is important because they impair animal health. General impacts include: despoilment and poor growth (internal parasites consume nutrients from feed in the intestine; external parasites suck blood, causing anemia and weakness, or irritate and damage skin); disease from organ damage (some internal parasites damage organs like the liver, or organ function, causing diarrhea); and disease transmission (biting external parasites can transmit infectious diseases). Every parasite has a development cycle from egg to reproductively mature adult, generally through egg, larva, and adult stages. The cycle can be direct — all stages happen within one animal (e.g. Ascaris) — or indirect, requiring two host animals to complete (e.g. Fasciola).
